title: Primitivity of the universal dual polarization
as_he_states: 59:11 expects the constructed polarization on the dual to be indivisible and generate the universal NS sections for the given degree.

title: Annihilator gcd versus canonical torsor trivialization

title: Albanese duality from a chosen abelian subfunctor

title: General separatedness of the correspondence functor
as_he_states: “I am convinced however that Corr is always separated” (57:23);57:32 asks the same question and proposes a fundamental-group specialization route.

state_of_art: Murre1965 Th4 assumes separatedness and records the unrestricted assertion as a problem; separatedPic of either factor is a sufficient case. Bertolin–Galluzzi Theorem1.1 supplies a semiabelian setting and cites Raynaud LNM119 III4.3; the exact latter proposition was not accessible. Modern Picard-space representability does not by itself verify the letter’s generic-constant-to-special-constant step for a nonseparated target.
why_open: No historical reason for abandonment is supplied. The bounded modern comparison has one explicit unclosed primary-source dependency, RaynaudIII4.3, and does not certify that the general question remains open in2026.
worth: High; read RaynaudIII4.3 and then test every hypothesis of the letter’s pre-ét rigidity argument.

title: Local Picard theory without regular puncture

title: Locally free conormal module and smoothness in characteristic zero
as_he_states: 57:64 asks whether a group scheme over a base with characteristic-zero residue fields is smooth along its unit when its conormal module is locally free.
plausible_today: Add the explicit local finite-presentation hypothesis along the unit, then the stated condition is equivalent to smoothness there.
state_of_art: SGA3 VI B Proposition1.6 states exactly this equivalence; the proof uses the invariant-differential pullback and the EGA IV smoothness criterion.
why_open: Settled in the later published theorem. No flatness assumption needs to be invented to apply that proposition.
worth: High historical value, low new-research value; align this question with Proposition1.6 and keep it distinct from the full Picard-functor question.
